## Fact check (new laws and rulings)

Status: HOLD

The post's central and repeatedly stated claim — that the 2025 Texas Legislature raised § 725.003 unsecured-load violations to a Class A misdemeanor (and state jail felony for injury) — is directly contradicted by legislative records: the only bill proposing that change (SB 1480, 89th Legislature) died in committee and never became law, and the statute's current text still imposes only a fine-only misdemeanor. Every argument in the post built on this premise (stronger negligence-per-se evidence, felony-weight civil evidence, insurance-defense claims being harder to sustain) rests on a law that does not exist.

- REVIEW: fact check CONTRADICTED: The 2025 Texas Legislature upgraded Texas Transportation Code § 725.003 violations to a Class A misdemeanor (and a state jail felony when someone is injured), strengthening civil negligence-per-se claims. (SB 1480 (89th Leg., 2025), the only 2025 bill proposing this upgrade, was referred to the Senate Transportation Committee on March 6, 2025 and died in committee on June 2, 2025, never passing either chamber. The current text of § 725.003 on capitol.texas.gov and FindLaw still classifies the offense as a plain misdemeanor punishable by a fine of $25–$500, unchanged.)
  - Source: https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/GetStatute.aspx?Code=TN&Value=725.003
- Confirmed: Texas Transportation Code § 725.003 violations were previously classified as a misdemeanor before the 2025 change.
  - Source: https://codes.findlaw.com/tx/transportation-code/transp-sect-725-003.html
